newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 12.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 12.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK's leading blue chip index suffered its first setback in more than a week, ending moderately lower on Wednesday as investors paused for breath. Having surged 137 points to record peaks during the previous six sessions, the FTSE 100 share index settled 21.8 points lower at 4,422.5, near the day's worst levels at 4,419.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares closed bourse trade sharply lower on Wednesday, with chemicals and drugs giant Hoechst AG to blame for much of the fall after a surprise move to pull a separate listing of its HMR drugs subsidiary. The DAX-30 index of leading German shares was 45.19 points down, at 3,415.40. In post-bourse trade the index fell 48.55 to 3,382.40.

PARIS - French stocks finished sharply lower on Wednesday as investors took profits on the market's gains ahead of the publication of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book and upcoming U.S. producer price data. Brokers said the market came under late pressure from weaker bond prices and an early fall on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 44.45 points to 2,641.70.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a volatile day marginally lower on worries about higher interest rate hikes, lower bond prices and an easier Wall Street opening. Dealers said demand by U.S. and U.K. investment funds for bank shares underpinned the market. "There has been a change of heart," a trader noted with respect to the renewed interest in banks. A weaker U.S. dollar also pressured some shares. Sentiment was nervous ahead of the March meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve with investors increasingly worried about an interest rate hike. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 5.87 points to end at 2,954.45.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended slightly lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit-taking pressure ahead of corporate book closings at the end of March. The market was briefly nervous after a series of statements in the telecommunications sector, but the impact was limited. The Nikkei 225 average closed down 85.45 points at 18,183.27.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks were dragged to a sharply lower close on Wednesday as investors sold down property counters on concerns about the outlook for the territory's property market, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index tumbled 133.07 points to 13,119.13.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower on Wednesday with fears on U.S. interest rates and Dow direction giving the big banks a drubbing. The All Ordinaries index closed 13.9 points lower at 2,454.4. Brokers said early losses were extended in the afternoon session as investors chose to move to the sidelines rather than commit funds with questions still hanging over Wall Street.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended Wednesday down, but markets broadly welcomed Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's first budget for seeking to reign in spending and easing foreign exchange controls, dealers said. The day began with most dealers on tenterhooks ahead of the budget speech. In the immediate aftermath of Manuel's presentation stocks ticked up across the board, but the reaction was seen as a knee-jerk response. With the all-share index nearing all-time high levels and a recent strong run on industrials, some profit-taking entered the market later. The industrials index lost 16.1 points to 8,368.6, but the all-share provded more resilient and ended the day up 6.1 points to 7,168.1. The golds index added 6.1 points to 1,447.5.
